TL;DR, I made an app that sorts the repos on awesome lists by trending stars, and it updates daily.

I'm not using AI to write this. kldjfklgjdcsjklxfhgjkshdfjkghsjkldfgyis8df7g897123hjkl23 See?

I use awesome lists to discover the best open source projects, but in most cases, the lists are not even sorted alphabetically, let alone by trending. However, the popular lists, like awesome-selfhosted, are updated pretty regularly.

11:00 UTC daily, I run a local worker to update all the repos, and redeploy the site.

And to be clear, I'm making no money off this. It's really just to scratch my own itch, and to buff my own work portfolio for job hunting. It's totally open source and if anyone wants to, I would gladly welcome contributions.

That's it. Enjoy!

Github: https://github.com/patrickclery/awesomer Live: https://patrickclery.com/awesomer/

story_text.value:
CLI tool for managing multi-project context workspaces in git with minimal effort and simple navigation.

Create a workspace with: camp create my-workspace

Convert an existing workspace to a camp: camp init

Give it a mission and a reason that it exists.

Load the shell integration with camp shell-init. Then csw my-workspace jumps to a workspace from anywhere on your machine. (Also supports switching between machines over tailscale with the same command)

Use cgo within a workspace to jump around your projects and context without typing long cd paths.

Commit your context from anywhere within the workspace with camp commit.

Add context linked commits to a project with camp p commit

Add -aw (auto write) flag to any commit command to write your commit messages in the background while you continue working.

title.value: Show HN: Camp version controlled context workspaces

story_text.value:
A registry of hand picked/built registry of ui/ux components so now i can produce slop without ai.
i always loved using and searching for ui components on every registry site that popped on my feed. i collected and saved all of these components but wanted to actually to build something thats more unique, free and easy to use.
i was hooked by ASCII components and my main focus was building also some of them and the results are really appealing (feedback is always appreciated), although i am working on even more and more unique.
there is an mcp and cli connection so your agent can easily search and use and component it finds interesting. there is also install by url and you can also get the prompt and also the code if you want to get only a section of the component.
my goal with it is to get more feedback on what looks actually good and what doesnt, because all of this is a one persons tase, and to get also the design community to use it and add to the component catalog.
if you have any question or feedback i would be really happy to listen/help!

story_text.value:
Over the past year, I found myself increasingly writing technical docs in Markdown. Unfortunately, there isn't an easy way to share and collaborate on these docs in real time.

I built Marble.md to solve this problem. Combining a minimalist Typora-like Markdown editor with real time collaboration. You can even connect your AI agents to do live edits. It support tables, code, LaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, HTML, and so much more.

Since it launched a month ago, it has been used by more than 1300 people already.

Give it a try and let me know what to improve :)

story_text.value:
Hello~! pocketty is an SSH terminal for iPhone and iPad, made for herdr. herdr keeps your agent panes alive on your computer and knows the state of each one: working, needs you, or done.

I made this in anger/desperation for the latter half of my recent paternity leave. Nap traps are sweet, but there's only so much doom-scrolling and movie-watching I can handle... In any event, I've been using it for the last couple months and no longer have to be my desk anymore to be productive. Now the nap-traps are still productive (when i want them to be) !

How it works:

- The app talks to your computer directly over plain SSH. Tailscale is the easy way to reach it from anywhere but any SSH host you can reach works.

- A small Rust daemon on the host watches herdr. When a pane needs you, it seals the alert to your phone's key with HPKE (X25519, ChaCha20-Poly1305). A stateless relay (pocketty's) on Cloudflare Workers passes the sealed bytes to APNs (Apple Push Notification servers), and a notification extension opens them on the phone. The relay can't read them and keeps nothing.

- Your SSH key is made in the Secure Enclave and can't be exported.

- The terminal uses libghostty-vt for state and draws with wgpu on Metal, so full-screen TUIs look like they do on your desk, albeit narrower.

- Diffs for each agent turn, a file browser, and previews of `localhost` dev servers your agent starts, all through the same SSH connection. No port forwarding to set up.

herdr and the daemon are optional. Without them, it's a normal SSH client.

There's no account to set up and no analytics or tracking in the app. The app runs a 14-day free trial, with full feature access. Then, if you're as happy as I am with it, then it can be yours forever with a one-time purchase: $99 for the first two weeks (launch promo) then $129 after that.

Happy to answer anything about the sealed push setup or running libghostty on iOS.

title.value: Show HN: Pocketty – iPhone SSH terminal that pings you when an agent is blocked
